scope.flow: GaugeV2 reward accrual and distribution when total staked supply is zero

statements.text: Users call withdraw or withdrawAll to remove all staked tokens from the gauge, setting _totalSupply to zero.
Time passes without any deposits while the gauge supply is zero.
During the empty period, notifyRewardAmount may be called by the distribution contract to add new rewards.
rewardPerToken is invoked while _totalSupply == 0 and skips adding time-based accrual, returning only the stored value.
The updateReward modifier advances lastUpdateTime to the current applicable time regardless of supply.
New deposits occur and users interact (e.g., via deposit) after the empty period.

Because lastUpdateTime advances past empty periods while rewardPerToken adds no accrual for them, subsequent notifyRewardAmount calls only consider leftovers from the remaining time, leaving previously skipped rewards unaccounted for and trapped in the contract's balance.
Entire epochs of reward emissions can become permanently stuck in the contract, leading to protocol fund loss without recovery.
When the gauge remains empty for an entire reward duration (one week), the full epoch's emissions become permanently unclaimable.
Even after new deposits and user interactions, the skipped rewards remain unaccrued and unclaimable because future calculations do not retroactively include the empty period's emissions.
Low-liquidity gauges that frequently empty may waste significant token allocations over time.
Reward emissions distributed during periods when total staked supply is zero should remain claimable by users rather than being permanently trapped in the contract.

ambiguities: Report does not state who triggers the updateReward modifier during the empty period or the exact ordering of notifyRewardAmount versus accrual calls.
Whether the full epoch's emissions are always lost or only when the gauge stays empty for the entire reward duration is conditional; preserved as potential.
No explicit unauthorized-caller or permissionless condition is stated; distribution contract is the described caller of notifyRewardAmount.
